title: Irregular Verbs: ferō, volō, nōlō, mālō
subtitle: Every tense of the indicative and subjunctive, plus infinitives, imperatives and the passive of ferō
intro:
These four verbs are irregular only in the present system (present, imperfect and future, and the present and imperfect subjunctive). Their perfect systems are completely regular: tul-, volu-, nōlu-, mālu- + the usual endings.
  • ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum is a 3rd-conjugation verb that drops the connecting vowel in a few forms: fers, fert, fertis, ferre, ferrem; imperative fer, ferte; passive ferris, fertur, feriminī. The perfect tulī and the participle lātum come from different roots.
  • volō, velle, voluī (want) switches between vol- and vel-: volō, vīs, vult, volumus, vultis, volunt; subjunctive velim (endings like sim), vellem.
  • nōlō = nē + volō (not want): nōlō, nōn vīs, nōn vult, nōlumus, nōn vultis, nōlunt. nōlī / nōlīte + infinitive means “don't …!”
  • mālō = magis + volō (prefer): mālō, māvīs, māvult, mālumus, māvultis, mālunt.

Watch out: the future 1st singular and the present subjunctive can look alike (feram is both), and the perfect subjunctive and future perfect share tulerit and tulerint. Latin → English lists every reading.
paradigmNote: Imperatives: fer, ferte · nōlī, nōlīte (+ infinitive). Infinitives: ferre, tulisse, lātūrus esse · velle, voluisse · nōlle, nōluisse · mālle, māluisse.
cue: Translate and parse: give every possible reading
